Hello group
I've been trying to run single species multi season occupancy models in unmarked using colext and am hoping someone can point me in the right direction. I have tried to seek answers from what seems like every past relevant thread but have been unsuccessful.

Over the course of 3 years I made repeated visits to camera trap stations and during those visits collected fruits. I want to relate those fruit collections to animal occupancy at those sites. I am trying to run these models with a subset of my data, using only 1 of those years.
For this subset, I have 42 sites, 7 primary sampling periods, and 30 secondary sampling periods. 
yearlySiteCovs = fruits collected
obsCovs = camhours for each secondary sampling period (30 obs for each site in each primary samp period)
siteCovs= forest type (a factor with 2 levels representing 2 different types of habitat)
Not all my sites have observations for all 30 secondary sampling occasions but after reading some past threads it seemed like I needed to add extra columns so that each site had equal length of secondary sampling periods. This has resulted in even more NAs than what I had and I suspect this may be an issue but I don't  know how to deal with it. 
The umf works when I run it, and so does running the constant model, but when I try to run a model with any covariate, I get an error message (see below). I also attached the data file.

camhrs<-as.matrix(md[,220:429]) 
md.y <- as.matrix(md[,2:211] ) 
md.y[is.na(camhrs)!=is.na(md.y)]<-NA
fruit<-as.matrix(md[,212:218]) 
forest<-md$forest

#standardized the continuous covariates
 cam<-scale(camhrs)
  fr<-scale(fruit)
  
  siteCovs<-data.frame(forest=forest)
  yearlySiteCovs=data.frame(year=fr)
  obsCovs=list(date=cam)
  
  md.umf<-unmarkedMultFrame(y=md.y,
                            siteCovs= siteCovs,
                            yearlySiteCovs=yearlySiteCovs,
                            obsCovs=obsCovs, numPrimary=7)
  summary(md.umf)

Can someone tell me what I am doing wrong? I know that each observation for the sampling covariate must have a corresponding presence/absence observation and I have checked over each site to ensure that they have the same #. The second part of the error suggests the opposite but I really don't get how to address the first part. Apologies if this is something really obvious or if I did indeed miss a previous thread on this.

parts:
Hi Alys,

I didn't dig too deep (and that error is a little cryptic), but I think this is simply because there's no observation covariate called "cam". If you substitute "date", your model runs, but I'm not sure that's the model you wanted.

Giancarlo

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: Error in V[!sites.to.remove[rep(1:M, each = R)], , drop = FALSE] / colext
parts:
Yes, the 24 is just the number of columns.

The line of code:

cmean.date<-apply(date,2,mean,na.rm=TRUE)

computes the mean date for each of the 24 columns (the 2 says apply the function over columns, a 1 would be by row), and loop just replaces NAs in a column with the mean of that column.

C
